+		RegistryStewardship
+		Registered suppliers and processors support our stewardship programs, which manage the recycling of electronics, tires, paint, and used oil materials. ARMA works with them to ensure environmental fees are collected, and materials are properly managed for end-of-life recycling.On this page, you’ll find information about registered stewardship suppliers and registered stewardship processors and how to register your business with ARMA.Jump to Supplier ResourcesJump to Stewardship ProcessorsStewardship SuppliersAnyone who sells, distributes, manufactures, supplies, or imports designated electronics, paint products (paints, coatings, and/or paint containers), tires (loose tires and/or tires attached to vehicles or equipment), or oil materials and filters in or into Alberta must register with ARMA.Register as a SupplierIf you are supplying or planning to supply eligible electronics, paint products (paints, coatings, and/or paint containers), tires (loose tires and/or tires attached to vehicles or equipment), or oil materials and filters in or into Alberta and have not yet registered, create an account by clicking on ARMA Connect and submit an online registration application.If your business is already registered with one of ARMA’s other recycling programs, you can register for additional programs through your existing account.Unsure if you are required to register or have questions? Please contact us at 780.990.1111 or toll-free at 1.888.999.8762.Supplier ResourcesFor more information for new/potential/prospective and existing suppliers, please see the resources below or visit our regulations.

ARMA regularly reviews them to ensure that they maintain the requirements of their respective recycling program.Registered ProcessorsBelow is information on the application process for becoming a registered processor for electronics, paint, tires, or used oil materials. Learn more about registered processor requirements in Alberta:Registered Electronics Processor Incentive Program RequirementsRegistered Tire Processor Incentive Program RequirementsRegistered Paint Processor Incentive Program RequirementsRegistered Used Oil Materials Processor Incentive Program RequirementsProcessor Application Requirements at a Glance
+                Electronics Processor Requirements
+		Comprehensive business plan including (a) details regarding how your company will obtain eligible end-of-life electronics (material must be sourced in Alberta); (b) ‘Downstream’ processors who will receive the metals, glass and plastic generated from the dismantling of the electronics for manufacturing into new products; (c) detailed revenue and expenditure statements, and projections demonstrating the viability of operations.Evidence of a closure plan and posting of security with Alberta Recycling; amount is calculated based on average monthly inventory (minimum amount of security is $20,000).Demonstrate that any processed material meets the minimum recycling standards outlined in the Program Requirements document.Copies of all required insurance.Evidence of an account in good standing with the Workers’ Compensation Board.Copy of Certificate of Recognition.Evidence of an Environmental Management System in place to ensure adequate control of the processing site’s impact on the environment.Please note that the review process for an application can take four to six months for interim approval to be considered.
+                Tire Processor Requirements
+		Comprehensive business plan including (a) details regarding how your company will obtain whole tires (material must be sourced in Alberta), (b) a description of the material that the tires will be recycled into, and an analysis of the markets for the material (c) detailed revenue and expenditure statements and projections demonstrating the viability of operations.Evidence of a closure plan and provision of security with Alberta Recycling; the amount is calculated based on average monthly inventory (the minimum amount of security required is $60,000).Evidence that the material processed from scrap tires meets the specification outlined in the Program Requirements document.Demonstrate that a minimum of 500 tonnes of tires can be processed without interruption and according to Program specifications.Copies of all required insurance.Evidence of an account in good standing with the Workers’ Compensation Board.Evidence of compliance with Alberta Fire Code (letter from fire inspector confirming processing site meets the fire code).Copy of Certificate of Recognition.Evidence of an Environmental Management System in place to ensure adequate control of the processing site’s impact on the environment.Please note that the review process for an application can take four to six months for interim approval to be considered.
+                Paint Processor Requirements
+		Comprehensive business plan including (a) details regarding how your company will obtain eligible paint and paint containers (material must be sourced in Alberta); (b) ‘Downstream’ processors who will receive the paint material for manufacturing into new products.Evidence of a closure plan and posting of security with Alberta Recycling (minimum amount of security required is $20,000) or provide evidence of security in place with Alberta Environment and Protected Areas.Copies of all required insurance.Evidence of an account in good standing with the Workers’ Compensation Board.Copy of Certificate of Recognition.Evidence of an Environmental Management System in place to ensure adequate control of the processing site’s impact on the environment.Please note that the review process for an application can take four to six months for interim approval to be considered.
+                Used Oil Materials Processor Requirements
+		Submit a comprehensive business plan including details regarding (a) how the company will obtain eligible used oil material (sources/generators of used lubricating oil, oil filters, and/or oil containers); (b) ‘Downstream’ processors who will receive the used oil material for manufacturing into new products; (c) financial information supporting the viability of operations.Evidence of a closure plan and posting of security with Alberta Recycling; the amount is calculated based on average monthly inventory (minimum amount of security is $20,000) or provide evidence of security in place with Alberta Environment and Protected Areas.Copies of all required insurance.Evidence of an account in good standing with the Workers’ Compensation Board.Copy of Certificate of Recognition.Evidence of an Environmental Management System in place to ensure adequate control of the processing site’s impact on the environment.For used oil, there is evidence of Safety Codes Council tank certification.Please note that the review process for an application can take four to six months for interim approval to be considered.

The relationship that Indigenous Peoples of Treaty 4, 6, 7, 8, and 10 have with the land is founded on a deep respect and relationship with the environment. +		The Government of the Northwest Territories (GNWT) contracted Alberta Recycling Management Authority (ARMA) to administer the revenue portion of their Electronics Recycling Program. ARMA is the main point of contact for companies (distributors) selling in or into the NWT.Distributor LoginRegistration ApplicationUnder the GNWT Electronics Recycling Regulations, any person manufacturing, selling or distributing electronics in or into the NWT is an electronics distributor (this includes retailers) as of February 1, 2016.All Producers Are Required To:Be registered as a distributor;Collect environmental handling fees on designated electronics sold/distributed;Report and remit fees, where applicable; andMaintain accurate books and records.If you are supplying or planning to supply eligible electronics and have not yet registered, create an account on ARMA Connect and submit an online registration application.Have questions?Contact us at nwtelectronics@albertarecycling.ca or toll-free at 1.888.999.8762.ResourcesNWT Product List and Fees (PDF)Remittance Overview (PDF)Remittance Instructions and Guide to ARMA Connect for NWT Electronics Distributors (PDF)NWT EFT Supplier Agreement (PDF)NWT Update Form – Registered REMITTER (PDF)NWT Update Form – Registered Distributor POP (PDF)GNWT Electronics Recycling Regulations (PDF)Letter from the GNWT to Electronics Distributors (PDF)Distributor Responsibilities (PDF)To learn more about the GNWT’s electronics recycling program, visit the Government of the Northwest Territories website.

-													Frits, chemicals
-													Frit is a mixture of inorganic chemical substances produced by rapidly quenching a molten, complex combination of materials, confining the chemical substances thus manufactured as nonmigratory components of glassy solid flakes or granules. This category includes all of the chemical substances specified below when they are intentionally manufactured in the production of frit. +    function initTooltips() {
+    // Remove title attribute from all  elements
+    $('a[title]').removeAttr('title');
+    // Iterate through elements with class 'tooltip'
+    $('.tooltip').each(function (i, v) {
+    var tooltip = $(v).val();
+    var columnName = $(v).attr('name');
+    if (columnName && columnName.trim() !== '') {
+    if ($(v).hasClass('orderable')) {
+    // For orderable columns
+    $('.lfr-search-container th > div > a').filter(function () {
+    return $(this).text().trim() === columnName;
+    }).contents().eq(0).wrap('');
+    } else {
+    // For non-orderable columns
+    $('.lfr-search-container th').filter(function () {
+    return $(this).text().trim() === columnName;
+    }).contents().eq(0).wrap('');
+    }
+    }
+    });
+    // JSP conditional logic for comments tooltip
+    // Initialize Bootstrap tooltips
+    document.querySelectorAll('[data-bs-toggle="tooltip"]').forEach(function (el) {
+    new bootstrap.Tooltip(el);
+    });
+    }
+    function initSearchTooltips() {
+    // Select spans with class fieldNameHasTooltip that don't already have a
+    // Bootstrap toggle wired up (e.g. search form field labels wrapped by
+    // LegislationListUtil.addTooltipToField).
+    //
+    // NOTE: we deliberately do NOT read/write the native `title` attribute
+    // here. Liferay's own core tooltip-support-web module (loaded on every
+    // page) also watches elements with a `title` attribute and converts it
+    // into its own `data-tooltip` system, stripping `title` in the process.
+    // That silently fights with Bootstrap's tooltip for the same attribute.
+    // Passing the text straight into the Tooltip constructor's options
+    // avoids touching `title` at all, so Liferay's module has nothing to
+    // claim.
+    var spans = document.querySelectorAll('span.fieldNameHasTooltip:not([data-bs-toggle="tooltip"])');
+    spans.forEach(function (span) {
+    var tooltipText = span.getAttribute('title') || span.getAttribute('data-tooltip');
+    if (tooltipText) {
+    span.setAttribute('data-bs-toggle', 'tooltip');
+    span.setAttribute('data-bs-placement', 'top');
+    // Remove whichever attribute is present so Liferay's tooltip-support
+    // module has nothing left to convert/hijack on this element.
+    span.removeAttribute('title');
+    span.removeAttribute('data-tooltip');
+    // Initialize Bootstrap tooltip with the text passed as a config
+    // option rather than read from a DOM attribute.
+    new bootstrap.Tooltip(span, {
+    title: tooltipText,
+    placement: 'top'
+    });
+    }
+    });
+    }
+    })();

+		Stewardship Recycling ProgramElectronics Recycling Program
+		How To Recycle Your Electronics&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2004, ARMA launched Canada’s first Electronics Recycling Program. Since then, this program has expanded to include more than 500 types of products. Use our depot finder to find where you can recycle electronics near you.When you bring in your electronics for recycling, they are shipped to ARMA-approved Registered Electronics Processors (recyclers). Registered Processors are private companies that have been audited and approved by ARMA.Electronics that can be recycled in Alberta include:Computers and servers Laptops, tablets, and notebooks (portable computers) Printers, copiers, scanners, and fax machines  Home small appliances   AV, telecom, toys, and music    Tools, lawn and garden     Visual display and all-in-one devices      Environmental fees help fund the recycling system for each stewardship program. For more information about what electronics you can recycle, please see our comprehensive list of products, definitions, and fees.Still have questions? Visit our frequently asked questions page or contact us.To register as a supplier of this material, please submit an online application.Please note that batteries embedded in electronics are accepted as part of the recycling program, but loose batteries are part of EPR's hazardous &amp; special products (HSP). “Alberta consistently ranks among the national leaders in electronics recycling, collecting volumes well above the provincial average.”2026 EY Economic Impact Assessment: Electronic Products Recycling Association (EPRA), provincial average of 10,623 tonnes.
+		Corporate and Institutional Electronics Recycling ProgramOld electronics take up valuable office space and pose potential security risks. With ARMA’s corporate and institutional electronics recycling program, you can recycle your electronics safely and securely. Use our depot finder to identify a recycling depot near you.Are you interested in using your electronics to raise funds for your initiative? Get your school, team, or club involved with the Electronics Recycling Roundup. The Electronics Recycling Roundup is designed to encourage schools, non-profit organizations, and community groups to increase awareness and ease of recycling while raising funds for their organization (or on behalf of an organization). Learn more about our Roundup programs.History of Electronics Recycling in Alberta Launched in 2004, ARMA’s Electronics Recycling Program was the first in Canada to recycle computer equipment, televisions, and select office equipment. These materials are often mistaken as “e-waste,” but they actually have significant value!On April 1, 2025, this program expanded by more than 500 materials, including power tools, microwaves, and musical instruments. This move built on the success of ARMA’s ePilot program, which launched in 2020 and allowed Albertans to recycle a broader range of electronics. By expanding the program, Alberta took a valuable step toward reducing waste and creating a more sustainable future.In addition to everyday electronics, Alberta is leading the way in recycling renewable energy materials, too. The province will be the first in Canada to develop programs for recycling solar panels, electric vehicle (EV) batteries, and wind turbine electrical components. As renewable energy continues to grow, these programs will be essential to managing waste and promoting environmental responsibility.The expansion of the Electronics Recycling Program and the development of renewable energy recycling initiatives are key to building Alberta’s circular economy. With support from the Government of Alberta and industry stakeholders, ARMA is helping to ensure that Albertans can responsibly recycle both current and future technologies, creating a cleaner, greener province.Over290,156tonnes of electronics have been processed since 2004How are Electronics Recycled?&nbsp;When recycled, components from electronics, including different metals, glass, and plastics, are used to create new consumer products. Recycling also allows hazardous materials such as lead, mercury, cadmium, beryllium, and antimony to be safely and properly handled, keeping them out of landfills.Environmental Fees for Electronics   Albertans pay an environmental fee when they purchase new electronics. These fees range from $0.30 to $2.75 and support the associated costs of recycling electronics. To learn more about the environmental fee for each electronic material, review our comprehensive list of products, definitions, and fees.Computers and ServersEnvironmental Fee (April 1, 2025 – September 30, 2026)$0.45Laptops, Tablets, and Notebooks (Portable Computers)Environmental Fee (April 1, 2025 – September 30, 2026)$0.30Printers, Copiers, Scanners, and Fax MachinesEnvironmental Fee (April 1, 2025 – September 30, 2026)$1.65Small Home AppliancesEnvironmental Fee (April 1, 2025 – September 30, 2026)$0.40 AV, Telecom, Toys, and MusicEnvironmental Fee (April 1, 2025 – September 30, 2026)$0.55 Tools, Lawn, and Garden EquipmentEnvironmental Fee (April 1, 2025 – September 30, 2026)$0.65 Visual Display and All-in-One DevicesIncludes televisions, monitors, and all-in-one devices (processing unit combined with a monitor). Less than 30″ screen size$1.30 30″ screen size or larger$2.75
